scenes.text: A newspaper may have called Alfred Nobel the merchant of death while he was still alive.
In eighteen eighty eight, his brother Ludvig died in France.
The story goes that at least one French paper thought Alfred had died instead.
It said he got rich by finding new ways to kill people.
Nobel invented dynamite in eighteen sixty seven, and held three hundred fifty five patents.
On November twenty seventh, eighteen ninety five, he signed his final will in Paris.
In fewer than one thousand handwritten words, he left most of his fortune to five prizes.
Physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace.
Some of his own relatives even tried to overturn the will.
It took about five years to settle the fight and set up a foundation.
He died in December eighteen ninety six, and the first prizes came in nineteen oh one.
Historians have never found that original obituary, so some think the story is a myth.
Would you rather win a Nobel Prize or invent something that changes the world? Tell me below.

title: The obituary that may have created the Nobel Prize 📰
caption: Nobel signed his will on Nov 27, 1895, leaving most of his fortune to five prizes. Legend says a premature 'merchant of death' obituary pushed him to do it, but no copy has ever been found.
